newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacia terminates Atrix license pact.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia terminates Atrix license pact.

text.p: Atrix Laboratories Inc said Monday that Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc, which recently divested the majority of its animal vaccine business, has terminated its license agreement for the animal vaccine development using the Atirx' Atrigel technology.

Atrix said that prior to Pharmacia & Upjohn making its decision to withdraw from this area of veterinary medicine, it had received several inquiries from companies seeking a delivery system such as Atrigel for animal vaccines and will pursue those opportunities now.
Atrix reported a first quarter profit of $0.39 a share, compared to a loss of $0.33 a share the previous first quarter.
The company said results in the first quarter of 1997 reflects the receipt of the first of several potential milestone payments from Block Drug Co Inc.

Atrix said it marketing agreement with Block Drug includes its first three periodontal products and that it anticipates additional milestone payments in 1998, based upon FDA approval of one of them, Atridox subgingival antibiotic therapy.

The company also said that based on the favorable results of feasibility work completed by Atrix earlier this year, Gensia Sicor Inc has elected to move to the next phase of activities in the two companies' efforts to develop a generic sustained- release version of leuprolide acetate for treating prostate cancer.
